leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open and none should be opened. The largest strategic claim in this ledger — that once the break began, leverage became safe for three weeks and the big defensive upgrade it had been tracking finally became affordable — does not survive its own arithmetic and has been corrected this run. A negative balance is penalty-free only until the matchday-five lock, and at that instant a negative balance scores nothing for the entire matchday. The only way back to positive is selling a squad player, because market-value gains produce no cash and the daily bonus is negligible over the window. At exactly eleven players there is only one sale available, because a second drops the squad below the legal minimum. So the real ceiling on any buy is cash plus one sale, which is a small fraction of the spending power the floor calculation prints. The upgrade that claim was built around fails that test by a wide margin even after selling the biggest saleable defender. The one exposure to diary: selling Sirch leaves ten players, which is safe now but becomes a heavy penalty if the squad is still short at the October lock.

binding_gap: Sirch is the binding gap and has been for several runs. He is fit but has never started this season, and with no bench he is fielded every matchday as a near-certain zero. The gap cannot be closed today. The only defenders cheap enough to buy without leverage are all confirmed bench players behind settled back lines, so buying one swaps a non-starter for a non-starter. The defenders who would genuinely close it are both Schalke starters in tonight's named eleven, and both are affordable on paper but not in practice, because the only sale that funds them is the sale that would also have to fund removing Sirch, and those are the same transaction. The gap therefore closes only when the squad holds a twelfth player or real spare cash.

verdict.headline: Quiet on points, one thing to do on value.
verdict.headline_short: Quiet on points, one thing to do on value.
verdict.detail: Quiet on points, one thing to do on value. The alarm this run appeared to carry — four squad players showing no matchday-four appearance, including the two most valuable assets — is a data artefact, not news: matchday four is still being played as this runs. Nobody is injured, nobody is dropped, and the squad is fielding its only legal shape. The single action is the standing Sirch sale, which has a hard cut-off tonight at the market-value update. Nothing on the board is worth the proceeds, so the money should sit rather than be redeployed today.

sell.reason: Sell Sirch, as already called. He is fit, which is not the reason — he is sold on selection and on value decay. He has no starts this season, only two late cameos, and he is losing value every day toward the floor price, so holding him to the October lock forfeits most of what he is worth now. The timing is the actionable part: wait for his kick-off this afternoon to confirm he is again not in the eleven, then take the instant sale before the market-value update tonight, after which he is worth less. Do not sell anyone else. ter Horst is losing value substantially faster than Sirch in absolute terms and is worth watching for that reason, but he is a confirmed starter, and at eleven players selling him without buying first drops the squad below the legal minimum.

buy.reason: No buy this run, and that is a considered answer rather than an empty market. The three defenders inside the affordable envelope were each checked against dated sources and all three are fit, none is suspended, and all three are bench players: one is an under-twenty-three promotion whose only appearances are substitute cameos, one is a fringe player returning from a spring operation who is behind a settled back four, and one is a genuine first-team signing whose own club news as recently as mid-September says he is still waiting for minutes. None of them would score more than the player being replaced. The two defenders who would improve the eleven are confirmed starters and are priced at exactly their market value, so price is not the obstacle; the obstacle is that funding either one requires selling a better player than the one arriving. The right move is to hold the Sirch proceeds and buy a starting defender when one appears at or below market value — there are nearly three weeks to do it in, and cheap bodies reach the board daily.
